title: GPU onboarding queue — capacity intake & triage (Nov 2025)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the working onboarding queue for new GPU capacity requests (Nov 2025). It is a working tracker used by Infra engineering to triage requests from Product, Serving, Applied ML, and Solutions Eng. The list below is intentionally lightweight — rows are updated during weekly triage and after stakeholder reviews.

How to use:
- Submit new requests via the Intake form (linked in INFRA-4821).
- Requests land in the backlog (Untriaged). Triage happens every Tuesday 10:30–11:00 PT.
- Assign staging priority, set provisional region(s), and mark approver(s).
- If the request requires Dedicated reservation or Private deployment capacity, tag with "dedicated" or "private" and add required compliance notes.

Triage rules (quick reference):
- Priority scoring: Critical (3) / High (2) / Normal (1) / Low (0).
- Critical: customer-facing outage, launch blocking, or legal/compliance deadline in <14 days.
- High: major feature launch or demo, sustained throughput requirement >100k tokens/min, or cost savings >10% for live workloads.
- Normal: ramping experiments, research workloads, non-blocking feature work.
- Low: exploratory benchmarking, ad-hoc spike requests.
- Regional constraints: prefer colocated region; if unavailable, fallback policies apply (see linked confluence).

Columns captured in this tracker (what we update in triage):
- Request ID: short id (e.g., ONB-203)
- Requesting team: Product / Serving / Applied ML / SRE / Solutions
- Owner: request owner (name + email)
- Use case summary: 1–2 lines
- GPUs requested: count + instance type (e.g., 8xA100-80GB)
- Duration: one-off | 4-week trial | ongoing reservation | spike (hours)
- Region(s): us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1, etc.
- Priority: Critical | High | Normal | Low (and numeric score)
- Deadline: date or N/A
- Approver(s): product / infra lead / security (names)
- Status: Untriaged | Pending approval | Approved | Scheduled | Denied | Deferred
- Notes: short freeform (cost estimate, blockers, opt-out recommendations)

Current queue snapshot (sample rows — live tracker kept in this doc for triage clarity):
1) ONB-203 | Applied ML | Owner: Miguel Torres | Use: eval+fine-tune for CCU model | GPUs: 4xA100-80GB | Duration: 4-week trial | Region: us-west1 | Priority: High (2) | Deadline: 2025-12-05 | Approvers: Priya Rao, Asha Patel | Status: Pending approval | Notes: needs KV-cache-enabled runtime; estimate cost $27k/month if extended.

2) ONB-207 | Serving | Owner: Zoe Wang | Use: new low-latency endpoint for chat service | GPUs: 2xH100-80GB | Duration: ongoing reservation | Region: eu-west1 | Priority: Critical (3) | Deadline: 2025-11-30 | Approvers: infra-ops lead, security | Status: Approved | Notes: will require dedicated pool and SLA; submit Dedicated contract addendum.

3) ONB-211 | Product (feature trial) | Owner: Liam O'Connor | Use: customer demo runway for Q1 pilot | GPUs: 1xA100-40GB | Duration: spike (72h) | Region: us-west1 | Priority: Normal (1) | Deadline: 2025-12-15 | Approvers: product manager | Status: Scheduled | Notes: scheduled in next maintenance window, use burst pool.

4) ONB-218 | Solutions Eng | Owner: Priya Rao | Use: on-prem PoC for regulated customer | GPUs: 8xA40 | Duration: ongoing private deployment | Region: on-prem | Priority: High (2) | Deadline: 2026-01-10 | Approvers: security, legal | Status: Pending approval | Notes: requires KMS integration and compliance checklist (see linked confluence).

5) ONB-224 | Research | Owner: Asha Patel | Use: benchmark quantization profiles across architectures | GPUs: 2xA100-80GB | Duration: one-off (3 days) | Region: us-west1 | Priority: Low (0) | Deadline: N/A | Approvers: infra team | Status: Untriaged | Notes: can be deferred if capacity tight.

Cost/estimates guidance (used by triage to score requests):
- Single H100-80GB dev unit baseline: estimate $X/day (see cost model, linked).
- For reservations > 4 GPUs persistent >30 days, assume committed discount discussion required.
- If request likely to change model type soon, prefer temporary spike rather than reservation.

Approvals workflow (concise):
1) Triage assigns priority + provisional region.
2) Infra owner prepares cost and capacity delta + schedules in backlog if approvable.
3) Approver(s) (infra lead and product/security if applicable) sign off in Slack thread and update ticket.
4) Scheduling team allocates nodes during weekly scheduling run.
5) Request reported in weekly capacity dashboard and included in monthly capacity forecast.

Open blockers / decisions required (as of 2025-11-18):
- Dedicated pool for eu-west1 has 6 outstanding GPUs reserved for internal churn; need decision to pre-empt for ONB-207 (action: Priya).
- KMS onboarding checklist incomplete for private deployments; blocks ONB-218 (action: Zoe + Security).
- Clarify cost allocation tag for Applied ML experiments where cost is shared across product teams (action: FinOps sync).

Action items (owners):
- Priya Rao: confirm Dedicated contract timeline for ONB-207 by 2025-11-20.
- Miguel Torres: update KV-cache runtime requirements and link PR to INFRA-4821 before next triage.
- Zoe Wang + Security: finalize KMS checklist and post to confluence by 2025-11-25.
- Asha Patel: prepare monthly capacity delta summary for Nov 2025 review.

Notes to self (working doc style):
- Keep rows short; long engineer notes live in linked JIRA tickets.
- If a request is denied, include reason and suggested mitigation in ticket and mark as "Denied" here.
- This doc doubles as the triage meeting agenda; update before Tuesday sessions.

History / provenance:
- Derived from the intake form responses and triage calls starting Q3 2025.
- Intentionally lightweight to reduce friction for requesters; detailed resource plans are produced only after approval.
